Definition: remote, literally or figuratively, of place or time; specifically, precious; often used adverbially (with preposition)
BiblicalUsage: Rachoq means far off — remote in place or time, and by extension, precious. God says, 'Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near'; Jeremiah says, 'The LORD hath appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love'; and the psalm says the LORD 'understandest my thought afar off.'
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me is that 'far off' is the measure of God's love: He loves from everlasting, He speaks peace to the far off, and He knows my thoughts before they are near.
